work_order.approach: THE TWO REJECTION OBJECTIONS, ANSWERED DIRECTLY. Objection 1 (money rendering): v3 pinned the ISO-code display form in tests/lib/money.test.ts and in qa_script steps 2 and 3. That is the currencyDisplay:'code' rendering; TR-23 requires the symbol. I executed the formatter in this repo's Node rather than judging by eye: new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US',{style:'currency',currency:'EUR'}).format(0) returns '€0.00' (symbol, the default), while only currencyDisplay:'code' returns the ISO-code form. This plan takes the compliant branch: formatMinor keeps the default symbol display and every pinned occurrence reads '€0.00' — the money unit test case, qa_script steps 2 and 3, and AC-2's how_to_verify. There is no ISO-code amount string anywhere in this document (the header 'Lisbon, trip, EUR' is a currency CODE label, not a formatted amount). formatMinor pins locale 'en-US' with no currencyDisplay override; verified outputs: EUR '€0.00', JPY '¥0' (0 fraction digits), INR '₹0.00'. BHD under the default display renders its code with 3 fraction digits, so the BHD test asserts maximumFractionDigits 3 and a '0.000' suffix rather than a byte-exact full string. Objection 2 (leave-notice offset): v3 asserted U+00B7 at codePointAt offset 17 of the RENDERED string 'You left Lisbon · Undo'. I computed it: that rendered string has U+00B7 at index 16 and U+0020 space at index 17. Index 17 is correct only for the TEMPLATE 'You left <group> · Undo', which is one character longer (<group> is 7 chars, Lisbon is 6). This plan names the two forms distinctly everywhere and the test asserts codePointAt(16) === 0xB7 on the rendered string. The companion em-dash case is 'Nothing here yet — add the first expense.' with U+2014 at offset 17 (verified by indexOf), asserted by codePointAt, read out of docs/ui.md line 123 rather than retyped. FOUR LAYERS, in dependency order. Schema: one edit to src/db/schema.ts plus one generated migration adding the group_type enum ('trip','home','couple','other'), groups, members and activity. Members gets a partial unique index on (group_id, user_id) WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL AND removed_at IS NULL (the removed_at clause is load-bearing: without it a re-add after removal is rejected with a duplicate-key violation; verified on this repo's PGlite); a partial unique index on (group_id) WHERE is_owner (exactly one owner as a database constraint); groups.invite_token unique for #5. Removal sets removed_at, never deletes the row (TR-16). Library modules: src/lib/access.ts is the authorisation boundary and the only module reading/writing group data (requireMember, readGroup, readMembers, listGroupsForUser, membership-scoped UPDATE predicates); src/lib/activity.ts is the only feed writer, callable only inside the caller's transaction; src/lib/money.ts holds formatMinor(minor: bigint, currency: string) with pinned 'en-US', default symbol display, bigint-only path. Actions: src/app/actions/groups.ts (create, rename, archive) and src/app/actions/members.ts (leave, undoLeave, remove) following src/app/actions/profile.ts exactly; ids via crypto.randomUUID() into .values() (no .returning(), TS2554 on the union); never redirect()/notFound() inside a transaction body (it throws NEXT_REDIRECT and rolls back to zero rows — reproduced). Screens: /groups/new, /groups/[id], /groups/[id]/members, (app)/not-found.tsx, and a home page listing the caller's groups. Judgement calls: (1) owner can never leave (broader than IAC-6's wording, flagged); (2) undo authorised by the feed (EXISTS member.left with actor_id = caller) plus NOT EXISTS guard against a second active membership; (3) IAC-2/IAC-9 conflict resolved by excluding group.* lifecycle kinds from the overview block; (4) settled sentence pinned verbatim from docs/ui.md line 165 (ASCII U+0027); (5) AC-9 names all four activity kinds with member.joined asserted on undoLeave. ARBITER AMENDMENTS (v5). The diagnosis stands; these change the plan where the critique was right. (a) Test path: the component test lives at tests/components/group-screens.test.tsx in files[] as well as tests[] — the src/ path vitest never collects is gone. (b) Refusal shape: member-excluded and non-member action calls return typed {ok: false} with no data and unchanged rows; 404 appears only for pages, matching IAC-4's refused and IAC-7's intent under the established action shape. (c) Undo authorisation: the guard is the latest membership activity for the row being a self-authored member.left, closing the leave-undo-remove-undo restoration against the owner's decision; the three-step sequence is a case. (d) removeMember excludes the caller's own row. (e) Activity reads go through readRecentActivity in access.ts, membership-joined, group.* excluded, newest first. (f) Balances are literal 0n through formatMinor everywhere, asserted as the rendered zero. (g) Home has exactly one h1 in both branches. (h) The leave notice name is server-resolved with a ten-second server-side render gate plus the client hide timer. (i) Second-user refusal cases cover every group and member action and are named in AC-7. (j) The migration and its journal entry come from one generate command, never a hand-edit. (k) qa_script no longer sends QA to confirm a dialog in a profile that cannot render one.

work_order.confidence_rationale: The proposal's executed verifications (formatter outputs, codepoint offsets, index predicates, transaction rollback, Tx typing) carry over untouched, and every accepted critique finding was re-checked against the code or the issue text rather than taken on trust — the two genuine bugs (stale undo, self-removal) reproduce against the specified guards. Below the 90 band for three reasons: the new guard predicates (latest-activity undo, ten-second leave gate, caller-id exclusion) are specified precisely but not execution-verified the way the v4 mechanisms were; the owner-leave reading and the IAC-2/IAC-9 exclusion remain interpretations a reviewer could overturn; and the refusal-shape call on actions interprets IAC-7 rather than deriving from it. Upward if both suites pass first run with the new cases green; downward if the guard edge cases (created_at ties) or the narrow owner-leave reading prove out.
work_order.debate_summary: The critique is largely right, and this work order is the proposal with its valid findings folded in — not a split of the difference. Blocking (dual test path): accepted and fixed; I re-checked vitest.config.ts and both paths myself, and the files[] path is indeed never collected. AC-4 404: accepted; IAC-4 says "refused both" with no status and the action shape returns typed results, so the 404 was invented — dropped from the check. IAC-7 action half: gap accepted, prescription corrected — the critique asked for NEXT_NOT_FOUND assertions, which contradict the typed-result action shape the plan (rightly, per the profile.ts precedent) mandates; the added cases assert refusal with no data and unchanged rows instead, recorded in alternatives_considered. AC-8 balance source: accepted; zero-ness was "by construction" with no named writer — balances are now literal 0n in the readers through formatMinor, asserted as rendered strings. Leave-notice two sources plus ten seconds: accepted; ?left= is now id-only, the name server-resolved, and a server-side ten-second render gate backs the client timer so a reload cannot resurrect the row. Missing activity reader: accepted; readRecentActivity added to access.ts with cases, which also closes the hole it would have left in AC-7's structural claim. Stale undo guard: accepted — this is a genuine authorisation bug (leave, undo, owner-removal, undo restores against the owner), fixed by the latest-activity guard with the three-step case. Missing non-empty home h1: accepted against TR-24 and ui.test.tsx; GroupList gains its own h1 with a composition case per branch. Owner self-removal: accepted — a genuine hole (the one-owner index does not catch a removed owner row); removeMember excludes the caller's row with a case. Unreachable browser confirmations: accepted; qa_script no longer claims a second-profile dialog that profile cannot render, and the confirmation half is component-tested here with browsers deferred to #5. Both minors accepted: the secondary row ships Members-only (recorded in out_of_scope) and the journal entry comes from the generate command, never a hand-edit (migrate.ts throws on tag mismatch). Of the missed edge cases I folded in two: two-member screen states as component cases with hand-built props, and name-boundary cases (trim, whitespace-only, 80/81 chars). Four I deliberately did not fold: double-submit guards (no criterion demands them; residual risk), back-button-after-leave (same code path as the existing non-member-404 case), rename-promoting-the-home-order and unauthenticated deep-link ordering (recorded as residual risks for #6), and refusing non-ISO currency codes (no criterion asks for an ISO list; the [A-Z]{3} schema stands). Of the regression risks, the migrations-test rename, the not-found wording inheritance and the #5 partial-index contract are folded in; home-becoming-dynamic, loading-skeleton debt and grep-enforcement were already in the order's risks. No finding contradicts plan/brief.md's recorded expense-core decisions, so none was dismissed on those grounds — and nothing was silently ignored.
